summary: Read the German Tractatus (Preface, 4.003, 4.01, 4.11-4.112, 6.4-6.522, 7) from the Gutenberg #5740 LaTeX source and the Lecture on Ethics from the Wittgenstein Project, with the traditional and resolute readings reported in SEP Wittgenstein §2.4. 6.53-6.54 left to #1008. Findings: the Tractatus is a meaning-theoretic rival to the arguability of natural theology only on its traditional reading, and only as an unattributed reconstruction from 4.003, 4.11, 6.42 and 6.432 (none states it); on the resolute reading it is no thesis. No route premise states arguability, so no route leaf gains a rival. The Lecture on Ethics holds that the expression of wonder at the world's existence is nonsense because its non-existence is unimaginable, and says that 'God created the world' referred to that experience; extending this to the statementhood of 'the world exists' (a candidate F2) is an unattributed reconstruction needing a bridge from the imaginability condition for wonder to a condition of sense for existence assertions, not recorded. Lean: not built. The bipolarity point (a sentence true in every possibility has no sense) is a two-line unfolding with no real logical content; recording it would be decorative.
blocker: The Lectures and Conversations on Religious Belief (1938; ed. Barrett 1966) are students' notes in copyright with no hosted copy; they enter only as SEP-RELIGIOUS-LANGUAGE §4.2 reports them.
